statement: If two connected graphs have isomorphic line graphs, then the two graphs are themselves isomorphic.
definitions: Graphs are finite and simple; the line graph L(G) has the edges of G as vertices, two adjacent iff the edges share an endpoint.
ground_truth_witness: The triangle K3 (vertices {0,1,2}, edges {0-1, 1-2, 0-2}) and the star K1,3 (center 0 with leaves 1,2,3). Each graph has exactly three edges and in each graph every two edges share an endpoint, so both line graphs are triangles and hence isomorphic to one another; but K3 and K1,3 are not isomorphic - they do not even have the same number of vertices. This is the unique exceptional pair in Whitney's isomorphism theorem.
